libtorrent.identity_note: The recorded full source identity is retained separately from the generated version-header marker. Each listed source file was byte-checked against the exact release archive; installed header bytes matched those members. No identity is inferred from a short version marker.

scope.implemented_domain: One experimental owned libtorrent session per continuation operation; peer-transfer payload plus protocol only.
scope.original_context: Original GlobalManagerStats spans its manager lifetime, with separate data/protocol counters and10-second rate averages. GeneralStats saved lifetime/mark/session uptime are different services. This milestone does not substitute one operation for those application-wide domains.
scope.placement: Statistics > Transfers > Current, explicitly identified owned transfer engine section. Existing Activity remains a separately labelled per-transfer payload series.
scope.no_implicit_start: Opening or refreshing Statistics does not create an engine or start a transfer. Observations come only from an already authorized experimental continuation.

metrics.lookup: Resolve the four exact names through session_stats_metrics at runtime. Require counter type, distinct nonnegative indices and bounds in the actual session_stats_alert counters span. Do not hardcode version-dependent offsets.

received.domain: Peer payload plus protocol received by this engine session

sent.domain: Peer payload plus protocol sent by this engine session

payloadReceived.domain: Payload received by this engine session

payloadSent.domain: Payload sent by this engine session

derived_protocol.admission: All raw counters nonnegative, combined>=payload. Checked differences, never inferred from raw rate subtraction.

metrics.avoid_double_count: Combined counters already include payload. Never add payload again or combine the separate excluded domains into these totals.
metrics.not_torrent_status_totals: Torrent status cumulative counters can reset at pause/resume. The sampler uses actual session cumulative counters, not sums of resettable torrent counters or integrals of sampled rates.

accumulator.ownership: A fresh primitive-owned accumulator for each actual engine owner; copies have independent state and results borrow no alert memory.
accumulator.counter_admission: All4 raw totals and both derived protocol totals must be monotone within one accumulator.
accumulator.time_admission: Caller-supplied steady observation nanoseconds are nonnegative and strictly increase after first acceptance.
accumulator.first_observation: Known cumulative totals, elapsedNanoseconds0, rates unavailable. Initial totals need not be zero; no prior rate is invented.
accumulator.elapsed: Nanoseconds since FIRST accepted observation, not engine construction, application uptime, wall time or saved mark time.
accumulator.interval_rates: Exact floor(deltaBytes*1000000000/deltaNanoseconds) for received,sent,payloadReceived,payloadSent,protocolReceived,protocolSent; use the last accepted interval, not total elapsed.
accumulator.integer_policy: Overflow-safe integer arithmetic with no floating approximation, signed overflow, saturation, unchecked wide product or compiler-specific integer extension.
accumulator.unrepresentable_rate: If any of6 exact rates exceeds signed64, the whole rate group is unavailable. Accept the valid totals/time as the next baseline; never replace the rate withzero or reject those facts as a reset.
accumulator.snapshot_validation: Raw counters and elapsed are nonnegative, combined>=payload. Present rates require positive elapsed; each direction has nonnegative components with payload+protocol<=combined and difference0..1 from independent floors. Validation uses safe differences instead of overflowing sums. Structural validation is not proof of provenance.

sampling.clock: Native std::chrono::steady_clock observations; supported Linux clock representation is compile-time checked as signed integral nanoseconds fitting int64.
sampling.alert_clock_not_used: Libtorrent2.0.12 alert timestamp uses high_resolution_clock, not a guaranteed steady clock. It is not used for native interval arithmetic.
sampling.explicit_stage_request: Initial/final-stage requests may bypass ordinary cadence. Multiple force requests while outstanding coalesce into one next post.
sampling.alert_consumer: The same existing popped alert batch feeds the sampler in all3 single-file and all3 multifile waits; no second pop consumer or changed transfer/error predicate.
sampling.borrowed_lifetime: Copy only the four primitives before the next alert pop. No alert pointer or counters span crosses into a queued GUI callback.
sampling.absent_callback: No metric query, clock read, statistics post or alert scan.
sampling.optional_error: Metric, bounds, clock, counter-discontinuity, post or observer exception disables this sampler without throwing into the transfer. Callback target remains owned until ordinary owner-thread destruction.
sampling.lost_response: A dropped-session-stats notification or unexpected response disables optional sampling. A lost response without a reported drop can remain outstanding; no retry flood or fabricated replacement measurement.
sampling.no_extra_final_wait: A stage request may be answered during the existing flush wait. Completion never waits for a statistics alert and adds no new deadline, sleep or final-total guarantee.
sampling.observer_precondition: Observation callbacks remain bounded owner-thread callbacks. Exception isolation is not a guarantee against arbitrary blocking/destructive caller code.

publication_and_cache.identity: Immutable nonzero profile session, per-operation identity, increasing sequence and original library target. Window admits a new Preparing only against a current target; same-hash later runs remain distinct owners.

states.Preparing: Run intent only; no observed engine-counter evidence.
states.Ended: Owner operation resolved successfully or unsuccessfully; retain last actual observation if available, otherwise explicitly unavailable.

publication_and_cache.delivery: Observed packets can coalesce to the newest owned sample; Preparing/Ended lifecycle boundaries are separately queued. Stale session/operation/sequence/target and post-terminal same-operation packets are rejected.
publication_and_cache.terminal_time: No synthetic zero or new rate observation after owner destruction. Last observed values need not include every byte of teardown traffic. They remain labelled last observed after completion/cancellation/failure.
publication_and_cache.close_reopen: Window retains at most the latest owned operation packet independently of the page; close/reopen can display that actual cached sample. A new operation or profile discards earlier facts rather than stitching/resetting counters into a false lifetime total.
publication_and_cache.saved_values: Engine telemetry never writes BiglyBT.statistics, changes saved mark baselines or reinterprets per-download saved counters as engine/application totals.
publication_and_cache.UI_rates: Transfers displays measured combined receive/send interval rates; the typed snapshot also owns payload/protocol rate components. No first-rate zero is inferred.
publication_and_cache.hidden_view: Cache owned updates while hidden/minimized; render only when the relevant page/subtab is visible. No extra idle sampler or animation timer.
